pr_title: Add MappedActionFilters for efficient action filters
pr_body:
ActionFilters are applied linearly, and for all actions. Yet many times an action filterly wants to be applied to a single action, and not invoked when other actions are processed. This commit adds a new special kind of action filter, a MappedActionFilter, which applies to a single action name. The MappedActionFilters are collected just as normal action filters during startup, but are then held in a hash map for quick access when processing action filters at runtime.

Some implementation notes: MappedActionFilters all run at the same action filter order, 0. Relative to each other, if more than one MappedActionFilter exists for the same action name, they are run in definition order (which should be considered effectively arbitrary).

closes #99784

issue_context.title: `ApiFilteringActionFilter` does a (recursive) linear search for actions to filter
issue_context.body:
Seen in an exception stack trace: we are wrapping `ApiFilteringActionFilter` around itself many times, once per filtered action, so effectively every action is doing a linear scan of the filtered actions, implemented recursively. I'm pretty sure a hashmap would be more efficient, and would avoid inflating the stack so much too.

comments:
This is unfortunately how action filters work at the moment. This is not recursive, note that there is a proceed call, followed by the apply of the filter. Proceed is how the chain is traversed. So each of these pair of frames is one instance of an ActionFilter.

The root of the problem is the lack of specificity when registering an ActionFilter. All ActionFilters are global, they don't have any notion of applying only to some actions. Thus when the action filters are collected, they are formed into a linear chain that must be searched.

TBC, we should fix this. But it will require re-engineering how action filters are both registered and invoked.

:+1:

I was thinking more that for `ApiFilteringActionFilter` specifically we should be able to move to a single `ActionFilter` instance which holds a map of the individual filters keyed by action name, from which it does a single lookup each time through. Clearly some engineering effort to change how these API filters are registered.

That sounds possible, but it will still require some re-engineering since currently the ApiFilteringActionFilter is what is returned by each plugin. We would need an SPI API for registering these implementations (might be tricky since they have dependencies), then have a single plugin return the main action filter.

While the above might be doable, I wonder if there is a middle ground where a "mapped action filter" concept is added, which ApiFilteringActionFilter implements. Then in server we can do the meta mapping within a single action filter, where we collection all the action filters that are mapped, and shove them into one filter. I'll play with this idea.

review_comments: Out of curiosity: I have seen this pattern elsewhere in our code base. Is this to use the HashMap as a "builder", and then store an immutable collection? Is it better than `Collections.unmodifiableMap()`?

Map.copyOf builds a brand new map which is immutable. Collections.unmodifiableMap returns a delegated map. The latter will incur an additional indirection on every access. Using Map.copyOf is trading off runtime cost for one time startup cost.

I don't want to complicate the action plugin interface. The above design has an extra level of indirection. It also allows plugins to do funny things like hold onto the registrar and then callback later. What would we expect then?

While I understand the dislike for the cast, I found it necessary in this case because we are trying to fit in within the existing action filters hierarchy. A MappedActionFilter _is_ an ActionFilter, it's just a special case.

> funny things like hold onto the registrar and then callback later

Yeah, that would be really bad and require extra care from the implementation (like using internal state to throw if it "survives" beyond the desired scope). 
Fair enough on the cast; if there was a better way of doing it I would have tried it, but if it's necessary no big deal.
